scenario.name: Microsoft IR & CISA AA23-320A DFIR — M365 Purview Unified Audit Log MailItemsAccessed & New-InboxRule Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a corporate mailroom intrusion reconstructed through three distinct security-desk receipts: first, catching the intruder quietly installing a hidden mail-sorting chute that diverts security alerts straight into the trash bin; second, reading the exact barcode scans that distinguish whether the intruder opened specific letters one by one or synced an entire mailbag at once; and third, uncovering a rogue automated courier pass left behind so the intruder can keep reading mail even after the victim changes their password. In this scenario (T1564.008, Microsoft IR & CISA AA23-320A DFIR, M365 Purview Unified Audit Log MailItemsAccessed & New-InboxRule Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: stealthy Exchange Online Inbox Rule Creation, then mailbox Search, then oAuth App Consent Persistence. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Stealthy Exchange Online Inbox Rule Creation, then Mailbox Search, then OAuth App Consent Persistence, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1564.008 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Stealthy Exchange Online Inbox Rule Creation (UAL Operation="New-InboxRule")
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1564.008 - Hide Artifacts: Email Hiding Rules)
stages.description: Right after slipping into an executive mailbox, the intruder bolts a silent auto-sorting rule onto the inbox so any invoice disputes or security warnings automatically mark themselves read and vanish into an obscure back drawer. To hide incoming security alerts and wire-transfer replies from the mailbox owner while forwarding copies externally, the actor invokes New-InboxRule via OWA. The Microsoft Purview Unified Audit Log records Operation="New-InboxRule" with Parameters showing SubjectContainsWords="Invoice,Wire,MFA", MoveToFolder="RSS Subscriptions", MarkAsRead="True", and ForwardTo (logged in Network Event 1 with AuditWorkload=Microsoft Purview Unified Audit Log , Exchange, Operation=New-InboxRule, ClientIpAddress=198.51.100.91, RuleParameters=SubjectContainsWords="Invoice;Wire;MFA" -> MoveToFolder="RSS Subscriptions" so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations New-InboxRule,Set-InboxRule,UpdateInboxRules (which invokes Microsoft 365 Exchange Online / Graph API operations to silently read victim mailbox items , MailItemsAccessed or create hidden inbox forwa so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1564.008 during "Stealthy Exchange Online Inbox Rule Creation , UAL Operation="New-InboxRule"" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact UAL Parameters: Name=".”, SubjectContainsWords="Invoice;Wire;Security", MoveToFolder="RSS Subscriptions", MarkAsRead="True" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , UAL Parameters: Name=".”, SubjectContainsWords="Invoice;Wire;Security", MoveToFolder="RSS Su so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1564.008 during "Stealthy Exchange Online Inbox Rule Creation , UAL Operation="New-InboxRule"" , To hide incoming security alerts and wire-transfer replies from the mailbox owner while forwarding copies externally, the actor invokes New-InboxRule via OWA while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ UAL New-InboxRule Mailbox=cfo@corp.com MoveToFolder="RSS Subscriptions" MarkAsRead=True / ⇠#1 RESP 1) from Node ① (#1 Hijacked OWA / Graph Session) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 MailItemsAccessed (Sync/Bind)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Mailbox Search & Item Access Attribution via MailItemsAccessed (Bind vs Sync)
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1114.002 - Email Collection: Remote Email Collection)
stages.description: To determine whether the intruder merely peeked at three contracts or hauled away the entire executive inbox, investigators examine the mailroom barcode ledger, which marks individual letter opens differently from bulk folder synchronizations. Next, the actor searches the mailbox for "password", "contract", and "routing number" and opens matching messages. Exchange Online Advanced Auditing records Operation="MailItemsAccessed" containing OperationProperties (MailAccessType="Bind" for individual item reads or "Sync" for bulk folder synchronization), Folders.FolderItems.InternetMessageId, and Folders.Path ("/Sent Items") (logged in Network Event 2 with Operation=MailItemsAccessed, MailAccessType=Bind , Direct Message Read, FolderPath=/Sent Items, InternetMessageId=<91a8b204@corp.com> , 482,910 bytes so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations MailItemsAccessed -FreeText "198.51.100.91" (which invokes Microsoft 365 Exchange Online / Graph API operations to silently read victim mailbox items , MailItemsAccessed or create hidden inbox forwa so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1114.002 during "Mailbox Search & Item Access Attribution via MailItemsAccessed , Bind vs Sync" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact UAL Field: OperationProperties.MailAccessType = "Bind" | IsThrottled = "False" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , UAL Field: OperationProperties.MailAccessType = "Bind" | IsThrottled = "False" via System / so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1114.002 during "Mailbox Search & Item Access Attribution via MailItemsAccessed , Bind vs Sync" , Next, the actor searches the mailbox for "password", "contract", and "routing number" and opens matching messages while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ UAL MailItemsAccessed (MailAccessType=Bind) on cfo@corp.com /Sent Items / ⇠#2 RESP 2) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Exchange Online REST / EWS), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 MailItemsAccessed (Sync/Bind)).

keySpecs.value: Verify that MailItemsAccessed auditing is enabled on all Exchange Online mailboxes and monitor IsThrottled="True" (if a mailbox exceeds >2,500 binds in 24 hours, assume the entire mailbox was accessed).

stages.title: Stage 3: OAuth App Consent Persistence (Operation="Consent to application") & Session Revocation
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1098.003 - Account Manipulation: OAuth Application Consent)
stages.description: Before logging off, the intruder approves a shady third-party mail-reader app carrying broad reading rights so that even when the executive changes their door key, the rogue app keeps slipping in through the side mail slot until investigators revoke both the app grant and every live session. To retain persistent API access to the mailbox even after the user resets their password, the actor grants OAuth Mail.ReadWrite consent to a rogue multi-tenant application, logged in the Unified Audit Log under Workload="AzureActiveDirectory" Operation="Consent to application" (logged in Network Event 3 with AuditWorkload=AzureActiveDirectory , Entra ID, Operation=Consent to application, GrantedScopes=Mail.ReadWrite, offline_access, ClientIp=198.51.100.91 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "Consent to application","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations "Consent to application","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant" via so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1098.003 during "OAuth App Consent Persistence , Operation="Consent to application" & Session Revocation" , To retain persistent API access to the mailbox even after the user resets their password, the actor grants OAuth Mail while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ModifiedProperties: ConsentAction.Permissions="Scope: Mail.ReadWrite, offline_access" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ModifiedProperties: ConsentAction.Permissions="Scope: Mail.ReadWrite, offline_access" via Sy so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1098.003 during "OAuth App Consent Persistence , Operation="Consent to application" & Session Revocation" , To retain persistent API access to the mailbox even after the user resets their password, the actor grants OAuth Mail while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ UAL Consent to application (Scope: Mail.ReadWrite, offline_access) / ⇠#3 RESP 3) from Node ③ (#3 Exchange Online REST / EWS) to Node ④ (#4 New-InboxRule (RSS Feeds)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 MailItemsAccessed (Sync/Bind)).

keySpecs.value: Restrict user consent to verified publishers in Microsoft Entra ID (Admin Consent Workflow) and audit all OAuth2PermissionGrant entries granting Mail.Read or Mail.ReadWrite.
